svg.title: Independent repetitions turn a normal threshold event into a binomial count
svg.desc: A normal measurement with mean one hundred and variance two hundred twenty-five exceeds one hundred fifteen with probability q, approximately zero point one five eight six five five two five three nine. The upper normal tail is shaded teal. Eight independent measurements from this same model have identical binary event probability q, so their number of exceedances Y is binomial with eight trials and success probability q. A separate discrete probability-mass chart shows counts zero through eight. The bar for exactly two is highlighted, with probability 0.2500. Retain the unrounded q in the binomial calculation. The upper vertical axis is continuous density; the lower vertical axis is discrete probability mass. Normal marginal distributions alone do not establish independence.
